I've been using the iPhone Air for the past year, and I recently switched to the iPhone 18 Pro about a week ago. Although both phones have their merits, my biggest takeaway from the iPhone 18 Pro is — absolutely no compromises. Allow me to elaborate.

iPhone 18 Pro: The most outstanding camera system, battery life, and performance

If you're looking to buy a new iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro is almost certainly a top contender.

The unit I've been using for a week is the wine red version, which replaced my iPhone Air. Although I love the Air, it's hard to match that "zero compromises" philosophy of the iPhone 18 Pro.

  • The iPhone 18 Pro's camera is significantly better than the Air's in both quality and versatility. The telephoto and ultra-wide lenses come in very handy in specific scenarios, and even the main camera performs better on the iPhone 18 Pro.
  • Battery life is equally impressive. During my time with the iPhone Air, I found the battery adequate for daily use but occasionally needed a midday top-up. After switching to the iPhone 18 Pro, I no longer have to worry about battery life at all.
  • Performance is also outstanding. The A20 Pro chip makes everything on the iPhone incredibly smooth, and Siri's AI responses are noticeably snappier. With the addition of a vapor chamber for cooling, the device has never overheated — something that occasionally happened with the Air.

I'm not a professional photographer, and if you want to see battery tests or performance benchmarks, my colleague Chance's iPhone 18 Pro review has all of that covered. After a week with the iPhone 18 Pro, the word "the best" keeps popping into my head.

The iPhone 18 Pro (along with the Pro Max) features Apple's most premium camera system to date, offers the best battery life, and delivers performance that surpasses all other models. I've also noticed some subtle improvements: the built-in speakers sound better, and the upgrades to the Dynamic Island are highlights.

All of the above are quantifiable differences, but what I also love is the peace of mind of knowing my iPhone is equipped with Apple's "top-of-the-line" hardware across the most important areas. No more wondering: Would family photos look better on a different iPhone? Would this stuttering issue not happen on another model?

Setting aside all the merits of the iPhone 18 Pro, I have to admit that I'm still very interested in the upcoming iPhone Duo.

The iPhone Duo, like the iPhone Air, isn't perfect but极具吸引力

The iPhone Duo shares a lot in common with the iPhone Air. Beyond the similar design language, both have their shortcomings.

Just like my iPhone Air, the iPhone Duo's camera system will fall short of the iPhone 18 Pro's. The battery might be comparable, but it certainly won't match the Pro Max, and sustained performance will likely lag behind as well. The iPhone Duo will also lack Face ID and the Action button.

However, despite these compromises, I'm still very much looking forward to trying this device in person.

Because it brings many innovative features that the iPhone 18 Pro doesn't have. The folding form factor could be the most significant hardware change in iPhone history.

This week I've been thoroughly enjoying the iPhone 18 Pro. But guess what? A few days ago when I picked up the iPhone Air again…

I immediately said: "Wow."

After a year of using the Air's slim profile, I've taken it for granted. But after spending a few days with the iPhone 18 Pro, I've rediscovered just how forward-looking the Air feels. I expect the iPhone Duo will deliver a similar experience — not just in design, but also in practicality.

I'm excited about the prospect of fitting an iPad-like experience into my pocket. Even though I'll have to live with the Duo's shortcomings, that anticipation hasn't diminished.

The era of Apple offering a single "ultimate" iPhone is over. If you want a zero-compromise device, the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are perfect. But if you're after a more forward-looking, more unique experience, I still can't wait to try the iPhone Duo.

Since Adobe launched Photoshop's generative AI features in 2023, I've been using them to remove unwanted objects and extend images. The results have been hit or miss for me, but these features are indeed much faster than traditional masking, clone stamping, and manual retouching methods. However, with the release of iOS 27, Apple has significantly enhanced the "Clean Up" tool and added a new "Expand" tool, so I'm curious how Apple's solution compares to Adobe's. Therefore, I asked a friend to help test both using multiple photos to see how big the actual difference in performance is.

For this article, my friend Jürg generously provided multiple photos he took during his travels in Switzerland and around Europe. His photography skills are far better than mine, and the subjects he photographs are much more interesting than what I get here in Ohio. You can see more of his photography on Instagram. I ultimately selected six photos: three for testing object removal and three for testing image expansion.

All photos were taken with an iPhone 17 Pro Max and edited on an iPhone 18 Pro Max running iOS 27.0. The "Clean Up" tool in iOS 27 offers three options: Auto, Quick, and High Quality. I kept it set to Auto for all three tests.

Photoshop testing was conducted on a MacBook Pro running Adobe Photoshop 27.10.0, using the "Firefly Fill & Expand" model. I used the "Object Selection Tool" or "Lasso Tool" to select objects, then chose "Generative Fill" with the prompt field left blank.

When using the "Expand" tool, I used the default expansion range in Photos. The "Expand" tool in Photos has limits on how far image edges can be extended, while Photoshop has no such limit. To keep test conditions as consistent as possible, I used Apple's Photos results as the baseline and had Photoshop generate images of similar dimensions.

I've done my best to keep the HDR effects consistent between photos edited in iOS 27 Photos and Photoshop, but there are still some minor differences.

Making things disappear

Right image: iOS 27 Clean Up tool

First up is the test of removing the red chair in front of the yellow door. This was the first photo I tested with the new "Clean Up" tool, and I have to say, it left a fairly positive impression on me. The result looks very realistic, and the only noticeable mistake I spotted was that the rivets behind the chair's left armrest were removed instead of being properly reconstructed. But I think most people probably wouldn't notice this, and it could be easily fixed by simply cloning them back in Photoshop. What particularly impressed me was that the shadow beneath the chair was replaced with a texture matching the surrounding scene, while preserving the original direction of light.

Right image: Adobe Photoshop Generative Fill

Photoshop performed worse than Apple's "Clean Up" tool in this test. The chair's shadow remained, looking more like an oil stain. The rivets on the door were misplaced, and one was clearly missing. The generated texture also showed noticeably more visual artifacts. Overall, its cleanliness and realism were far inferior to the "Clean Up" tool's results.

The "Clean Up" tool impressed me just as much in this test. Not only did it remove the plate with bread on it, it also added fairly decent reflections to the cup and jar. What's even more clever is that it also handled the spoon handle in the reflection with meticulous precision — the details are quite impressive. The "Clean Up" tool also completely erased the shadow the plate had left on the napkin. I had assumed removing a red plate from a red tablecloth of the same color would be a bigger challenge for the "Clean Up" tool, but that wasn't the case! If I had to nitpick, the "Clean Up" tool left breadcrumbs next to the plate, but that's easily fixed by running "Clean Up" on that area one more time.

Photoshop performed reasonably well at removing the plate with bread, but similarly handled the area with remaining shadow poorly. The napkin looks like it got stained or wet, but at least Photoshop didn't leave as many annoying crumbs as before.

This photo was a much bigger test for the "Clean Up" tool. After attempting to remove the man on the right, the "Clean Up" tool left a mess of patchwork marks with fairly obvious flaws. The leaves look overly rough. The situation on the left side of the image was similar — when the white-haired woman standing behind the white flower cluster was removed, the same difficulty appeared. Additionally, the "Clean Up" tool left a "ghost-like" remnant in the position where the dog's head had been. While you could barely say it blends into the stone wall, it becomes much more obvious in this side-by-side comparison.

Photoshop, on the other hand, effortlessly removed the woman on the left standing behind the white flower cluster as well as the man on the right hidden behind the leaves, while realistically filling in both areas. The end result was very realistic, looking as if no one had ever stood there. Photoshop also avoided leaving any ghost-like shadows this time.

Adding content to images

I think this photo of a winding, ancient staircase is a great test subject because I figured AI wouldn't necessarily figure out what was in the scene right away, so I was curious how both would interpret the scene and handle it. As it turns out, iOS 27's "Expand" tool seemed to read the photo as something resembling a ceiling fan, rounding off the end of the staircase into something that looked like a fan blade. Photoshop, on the other hand, simply extended the staircase outward, and remarkably, the wood grain matched up surprisingly well.

The "Expand" tool lived up to its name in this test. It extended the scene exceptionally well, producing a very realistic final image. Note how the windows were reasonably and repeatedly extended, and although the bridge on the right side of the photo looks slightly too smooth, the overall result still looks quite plausible.

Now let's look at Photoshop's work. Photoshop, did you actually try? This is a complete failure on all fronts — pure, blatant AI garbage output. The windows and roofline in the upper left of the photo are an absolute disaster. The bridge on the right doesn't have the realistic arch structure that Apple's version has, and most inexplicably, Photoshop had the waterfall change direction at will instead of extending along the original waterway.

The "Expand" tool again generated a realistic image that, while not perfect, was clearly far superior to Photoshop's. It created a believable table with books or magazines placed on it, and the flowers in the vase look much more realistic than Photoshop's. The decorative pattern above the door on the left matches fairly well with the actual pattern in the photo. However, some strange elements appeared on the right side of the photo, such as an extra radiator, a mysterious wire, and a table that appeared out of nowhere.

Perhaps the biggest difference between "Expand" and Photoshop lies in how the ceiling was handled. The "Expand" tool reproduced more of the wood grain from the opposite wall, while Photoshop tried to transform it into something resembling a structural beam.

As for Photoshop, it seems unable to generate an image free of AI slop traces. The table it generated has too many legs, and it looks as if it simply "broke off" and then blended into the floor. The decorative pattern above the door isn't realistic enough either, missing a "swirl" and lacking the textured paint effect seen on the actual decoration in the photo.

I wouldn't say either one is perfect, but in terms of realism, I think Apple's solution edges out Adobe's by a notch.

The good, the bad, and the AI garbage

It's worth mentioning that using Photoshop requires a subscription, but the features I used during testing do not consume generative AI credits. Adobe does offer the option to let users select other AI models that may require credits, but I did not use those models in my testing. Apple has also clearly stated that some Apple Intelligence features "may be subject to usage limits" and may charge for expanded functionality in the future.

It's clear that Apple has made major improvements to the "Clean Up" tool — a significant step up from previous iOS versions. I've tried it before and always found the performance mediocre, but now it genuinely does a great job. The new "Expand" tool is equally impressive, clearly outperforming Adobe's solution in my tests. Adobe offers unlimited revisions and the ability to adjust results through prompts, but if the extra generations and prompts just keep producing more obvious AI garbage, the value of these advantages becomes questionable. Apple may be more restrictive in this regard, but its first-pass results are far better to begin with.

Of course, actual results will vary depending on photo content, scene complexity, and what you're asking the tool to do. The above is simply what I got for the photos I tested.

What about you: Have you had a chance to try Apple's new "Clean Up" and "Expand" tools? If so, what did you think?

海莉·威廉斯（Hayley Williams）就前夫、新好萊塢（New Found Glory）結他手查德·吉爾伯特（Chad Gilbert）於周日因癌症離世、終年45歲的消息發表聲明。

吉爾伯特今年較早前透露自己確診第四期腎上腺皮質癌。這位音樂人早於2021年首次公開表示自己正與轉移性嗜鉻細胞瘤搏鬥，該疾病屬一種罕見的腎上腺癌症。

威廉斯周三在Instagram限時動態發文寫道：「一直不知道該說什麼，也不知道是否應該開口。但我現在確信我想說，因為生命正正由我們交錯的路徑所組成，而我們交會的原因無窮無盡。」

她表示：「查德確實是樂壇傳奇，與他相連的歲月教曉我很多事情。」她又寫道：「他介紹我認識的人，至今仍以美麗的方式塑造我的人生，還有他帶我接觸的音樂與文化，也讓生命豐盛得多。」

威廉斯續說，對於吉爾伯特對樂壇的貢獻，「該說的別人大概都說過了」，並補充指「他對建立社群那份熱忱令人敬佩，至今仍深深印在我心」。

她最後寫道：「我會永遠感激，因他讓我對硬核社群與文化有了更深的了解與敬意。」並以此作結，向其家人、NFG大家庭以及所有好友送上愛意與慰唁。

威廉斯與吉爾伯特於2008年開始交往，六年後訂婚。兩人於2016年2月結婚，其後於2017年7月宣布分開。

布魯克·霍根正在回憶她和已故父親浩克·霍根之間的關係，如何在其職業摔角手父親與她其中一位最親密的朋友發生關係後變得「日益複雜」。

38歲的霍根星期四接受《Us Weekly》雜誌訪問時表示，當她發現父親與她的朋友Christiane Plante發生性關係後，兩人之間的關係出現了「重大轉捩點」。

她說：「我很輕易就會原諒別人——有時候可能太輕易了——我原諒了他，但我們之間的關係在之後起了變化。我認為他再也無法像以前那樣看待我了。」

Plante在2008年接受《National Inquirer》訪問時，確認了她與浩克·霍根（本名Terry Gene Bollea）的關係。她告訴該小報，她與這位WWE冠軍的關係發生在其妻子Linda Marie Claridge已經「離開他」之後。

霍根聲稱，在得知妻子想離婚時他感到「震驚」，《Today》報道。Claridge於1983年與霍根結婚，並於2007年提出離婚申請，兩人的離婚於2009年正式生效。

布魯克·霍根告訴《Us Weekly》，父母婚姻結束後，「我們整個家庭結構都改變了」。

她分享道：「隨著時間過去，事情變得日益複雜，最終我一直相信可以經得起任何考驗的那段關係，再也無法承受周遭發生的一切。這可能是我最希望大家明白有關霍根家的事：公眾的觀感會將家庭簡化為英雄和反派。」

布魯克·霍根補充說：「真實的家庭並非如此簡單。」

她亦公開談及家族中「濃厚的愛」與「功能失調」之間的雙重性。

她聲稱，「恐懼、怨恨、巨大的背叛、金錢、名氣、形象管理以及數十年來未能化解的傷害」都在她的家中「同一屋簷下」共存，並補充道：「我可以深愛我的父親，同時亦能誠實說出他傷害我的地方。我可以感謝家人給予我的美好事物，同時亦承認那種動態最終變得令我無法再生活其中。這兩者可以同時成立。」

布魯克·霍根表示，她的父親在2025年7月24日因心臟病發去世，享年71歲，在很長一段時間內對她而言「仍是一位好爸爸」。

她說：「我和父親之間的根基非常穩固。這份根基經歷了公眾醜聞、私人痛苦、離婚、家庭的巨大轉變以及長時間的疏離，依然屹立不倒，因為在這一切背後，有一段真實而深厚的羈絆。」

續簽協議將於明年生效

說蘋果與高通的關係一波三折絕不為過。

兩家公司曾經是主要商業夥伴，但於2017年因高通的專利授權做法及專利費問題捲入一場大規模的法律訴訟。

簡而言之，蘋果於2017年初在美國聯邦法院起訴高通，挑戰高通的專利授權做法，並追討蘋果聲稱高通不當扣留、總額接近10億美元的專利費退款。

就在訴訟發生前三天，美國聯邦貿易委員會（FTC）亦起訴高通，指控其授權做法反競爭。投訴特別提及高通與蘋果的業務往來，聲稱高通提供數十億美元的條件式回扣，以換取蘋果在新款iPhone及iPad上獨家使用其 modem 晶片。

數月後，高通反訴蘋果，指控蘋果違反協議並干擾其與iPhone及iPad製造商的關係。

爭議於2019年落幕，蘋果與高通達成協議，同意撤回雙方在全球範圍內的所有訴訟。

作為和解的一部分，蘋果向高通支付了一筆未披露的款項，當中包括解決蘋果在訴訟期間扣留專利費的爭議。兩家公司亦簽訂了一份為期六年的全球專利授權協議，以及另一份多年期的晶片組供應協議。

該授權協議於2019年4月1日生效，當中包括一項讓蘋果可額外延長兩年的選擇權。蘋果最終行使了該選擇權，將協議延長至2027年3月。

高通今日宣布兩家公司再度續簽協議，新協議將於2027年4月1日生效。

以下是完整的新聞稿內容：

高通公司今日宣布與蘋果續簽全球專利授權協議，新協議將於2027年4月1日生效。高通技術授權（QTL）高級副總裁兼總經理John Han表示：「我們很高興能延長與蘋果的授權協議。」

高通未有披露續簽協議的有效期，而蘋果至今仍未就此續約作任何評論。

值得注意的是，今日的宣布與蘋果在iPhone上使用高通modem無關——這個議題近期備受關注，因為蘋果在美國版iPhone 18 Pro Max採用了高通modem，但在其他地區則使用自家研發的C2 modem。

蘋果尚未正式評論其未來的modem計劃，但外界普遍預期該公司最終將全面棄用高通modem。

A video of the Q&A session from one of Apple's most iconic events of the past 20 years has surfaced online — watch it before it's taken down. See the video below.

Watch before Apple takes it down

Even if you weren't closely following Apple news in 2010, you've probably heard of "Antennagate" — and the hastily arranged press conference that pulled Steve Jobs back from a family vacation in Hawaii.

If you're new to the story, here's what happened: shortly after Apple launched the iPhone 4, users discovered that the way you held the phone could cause a dramatic drop in signal.

The controversy was enormous, and Apple held an emergency event to respond just weeks after the iPhone 4 went on sale.

At the event, Jobs explained that the signal attenuation wasn't unique to the iPhone 4, and that customers could get a free case to avoid touching the antenna with their bare hands, or receive a full refund.

After the event, Jobs sat down for a Q&A session with then-COO Tim Cook and Bob Mansfield, who was then SVP of Mac hardware engineering.

There have long been various accounts of what happened in that Q&A — including John Gruber's recollection that he asked a question that prompted Jobs, Cook and Mansfield to pull unsheathed iPhones from their pockets, producing one of the more memorable photos of the era. But actual video of the session has never surfaced. Until now.

Earlier this week, a YouTube channel called Sir Mix-A-Lot Rare Music (which appears to have no real connection to the actual Sir Mix-A-Lot) uploaded the full 47-minute Q&A session, which you can watch below:

There's no information on how the channel obtained the footage, or whether Apple will issue a takedown. But now that it's out there, even if the original upload is removed, copies are likely to resurface elsewhere with ease.

The fact that the video is still viewable at the time of writing is a good sign. But if you want to witness this slice of Apple history for yourself, it's worth catching sooner rather than later.

再無特朗普大道。

加拿大首都渥太華嘅官員星期三一致投票通過，將一條以美國總統特朗普命名嘅街道改名。

今次行動距離特朗普喺同加拿大打緊貿易戰期間簽署行政命令、將安大略湖改稱「美洲湖」唔夠一個月，當時已引起廣泛批評（加拿大方面更加堅持用原名）。

特朗普對加拿大唔太友善嘅態度，令到改「特朗普大道」嘅聲音再次響起。呢條街位於渥太華中央公園社區，同區內其他街道一樣，喺九十年代末至二千年代初落成，當時以紐約市相關嘅地標、地點同人物命名。

65歲嘅退休人士約翰·杰爾馬諾接受《紐約时报》訪問時話，淨係收件地址呢件事就「好尷尬，好似被人恥笑咁」，「情況一日差過一日」。

其他當地人亦對呢個街名表示不滿，包括渥太華記者穆罕默德·亞當。佢喺本月初嘅《渥太華公民報》專欄中寫道，加拿大首都竟然有一條以特朗普命名嘅街道實在「令人費解」，因為對方一直「致力於摧毀呢個國家」。

渥太華市議員賴利·布羅克頓喺2021年1月6日美國國會山莊事件發生後幾星期接受加拿大HuffPost訪問時話，多年來一直有居民因為感到尷尬而想取消呢個街名。

佢話喺特朗普在任期間改名「唔合適」，因為擔心可能會「對加拿大帶嚟後果」。

佢補充話：「聽落可能好極端，但我覺得佢卸任之後先展開公開程序會更加合適。」

隨着拜登入主白宮，呢啲憂慮有所減輕，2021年嘅改名行動最後不了了之，加拿大廣播公司新聞報道指居民對改名「意見分歧」。

佢哋嘅顧慮明顯同改名帶嚟嘅「麻煩」有關，因為居民要更改駕駛執照、銀行以及其他文件上嘅地址。

布羅克頓上月底接受CBC新聞訪問時話，依家已經「冇得再拗」。

佢話：「我覺得係時候正視呢位總統造成嘅破壞同傷害，包括對我哋自己國家嘅影響。」

布羅克頓已經負責同街上65戶居民商討新街名，新名之後會喺明年交由市議會審批。

三藩市（美聯社）——加州最高法院週四裁定，一名共和黨加州縣警長必須交還他在去年一場特別選舉中沒收、超過50萬張選票，這些選票涉及一宗毫無根據的選舉舞弊調查。

河濱縣警長查德·比安科於二月從2025年11月一項特別選舉中沒收了大約65萬張選票。該項選舉涉及全州國會選區重劃，對民主黨有利，並由州長加文·紐瑟姆推動。這項提案在全州輕鬆通過，並在比安科所在縣以約8萬票勝出。

法院稱沒收選票的行為「非法」，並表示加州法律規定已投選票必須由選舉官員保管和控制，即使在刑事調查期間也不例外。法院在一致裁決中指出，比安科還必須「除遵守本命令所需的情況外，不得再處理選票」。比安科沒有立即就裁決作出回應。

法院寫道：「如果懷疑有選舉舞弊行為，《選舉法》為執法部門提供了多種機制，以便在不損害選票完整性的前提下審查和檢查選票。」

比安科對選票展開調查之際，總統唐納德·特朗普多次質疑2020年大選結果，並援引未經證實的舞弊個案。其政府於一月在喬治亞州一間選舉辦事處沒收選票及其他文件。部分共和黨人已在各州仿效特朗普有關選舉的言論。

選舉官員及公民權利團體一直密切關注比安科一案，以防特朗普或其支持者可能在11月試圖沒收選票。

比安科表示，他在收到一個本地公民團體投訴點票結果有誤後，將選舉材料扣押作為刑事調查的一部分。當地選舉官員此前已表示該投訴毫無根據。比安科當時正在競選州長，但未能通過初選。

民主黨籍司法部長羅伯·邦塔隨即提出法律挑戰，認為該警長對選舉材料無管轄權，並警告說沒收選票旨在煽動對選舉的不信任。他下令比安科交還選票，但比安科沒有照辦。

邦塔週四表示：「法院現已明確表明，這種抗命行為不能容忍，司法部長有權在警長採取不當行動時介入，而已投選票應由選舉官員保管。」

加州大學洛杉磯分校投票權利項目亦代表多名河濱縣選民，對該警長及河濱縣選舉事務處提出訴訟。加州最高法院上個月同時聆訊了這兩宗案件。

法院亦裁定，搜查令並不能凌駕於本州選舉法之上。

加州大學洛杉磯分校投票權利項目法律主任兼聯合創辦人查德·鄧恩表示：「法院的決定重申了一個基本原則——在加州，《選舉法》適用於所有人，包括執法部門。這些是選民的選票，必須透過立法機關制定的程序加以保護。這項裁決為全加州的選舉官員、執法部門及選民提供了重要的明確指引。」

紐瑟姆於週六簽署一項法案，將禁止任何人像比安科那樣沒收選票。

比安科在沒收選票後不久便開始重新點票，由警長辦公室人員在法院委任的特別監察人監督下進行，但數天後因面對州司法部長及投票權利團體日益增加的法律挑戰而暫停點票。然而他仍未交還選票。

代表比安科出庭的布拉德利·赫茨辯稱，該警長在接獲投訴後有法律責任展開刑事調查，並已依照刑法執行調查，於二月首先發出搜查令。

赫茨表示，比安科未有將選票交還河濱縣選舉事務處，因為這些選票屬於「證據」。

在沒收選票之時，比安科是兩名在競爭激烈的六月初選中競逐州長提名的主要共和黨人之一。他未能晉身大選，其後宣布計劃於2028年競選連任警長。

前州司法部長、民主黨州長參選人哈維爾·貝塞拉是加州大學洛杉磯分校訴訟的一部分，旨在制止比安科的舉動。

新奧爾良（美聯社）——聖路易斯鷹隊嘅得分手兼籃板王、1956年首位NBA最有價值球員得主卜比佩提（Bob Pettit）逝世，享年93歲。

佩提嘅母校路易斯安那州立大學（LSU）星期四公布佢於前一天離世，校方未有透露死因。

佩提喺LSU讀書時已係全美最佳球員，之後加入NBA，效力鷹隊嘅11個球季每季都入選全明星陣容。佢帶領球隊喺1958年總決賽擊敗當時嘅勁旅波士頓塞爾特人，奪得鷹隊史上唯一一個總冠軍。

佢亦喺1959年再次當選常規賽MVP，並四次榮膺全明星賽MVP，呢項成就只有洛杉磯湖人名將高比拜仁（Kobe Bryant）能夠媲美。

佩提活躍嘅年代，NBA有渣巴、羅素、奧斯卡羅拔臣、艾金比勒等球星。然而當時NBA仲未喺電視廣泛直播，加上佩提効力嘅係小球市，佢嘅曝光機會因而大受限制。

佩提前場高大，擁有六呎九吋嘅身型同205磅嘅體重，加上髮線嚴重後移，喺大前鋒呢個位置仲未成為籃球術語之前，已經係籃底嘅一巨大存在。佢好少缺陣，仲能夠擔任中鋒，係最早一批唔只靠背籃單打嘅高大球員之一。

佩提喺1955年贏得最佳新秀，當年係鷹隊喺密爾沃基嘅最後一季，之後球隊遷往聖路易斯。

佢喺下一個球季奪得MVP，以場均25.7分領銜全聯盟得分榜；1959年再以場均29.2分成為聯盟得分王。

佢喺1964–65球季結束後退役，職業生涯場均取得26.4分同16.2個籃板。當時佢係NBA總得分（20,880分）紀錄保持者，總籃板數（12,849個）則排第二。

1970年，佢獲選入奈史密斯紀念籃球名人堂。

名人堂嘅人物介紹寫道：「身形修長優美、體能狀態一直保持極佳，卜比佩提嘅體格令佢成為最早一批面向籃框打波嘅高大球員之一。但佩提最突出嘅係佢嘅決心——佢從唔肯畀人超越。」

羅拔李佩提二世（Robert Lee Pettit Jr.）喺1932年12月12日生於路易斯安那州巴頓魯治。佢爸爸從事執法工作，做過東巴頓魯治教區警長。佩提喺籃球方面屬大器晚成，去到高三先至打入巴頓魯治高中嘅校隊。

佢高三嗰年以隊長身份帶領巴頓魯治高中贏得州冠軍，獲得十幾間大學招手。佢選擇留喺屋企，喺LSU展開大學生涯，喺打嘅係二年級嗰年已經打出名堂——嗰個年代球員要等到大二先可以參加校隊比賽。

佢連續三季成為東南聯盟嘅得分王，二年級場均25.5分、三年級24.9分、四年級31.4分。

佩提係LSU僅有三位入選名人堂嘅球員之一，其餘兩位係皮特馬拉維奇（Pete Maravich）同沙奎爾奧尼爾（Shaquille O’Neal）。LSU主場、皮特馬拉維奇紀念館外面矗立住佩提前同奧尼爾嘅銅像。LSU退役咗佢嘅50號球衣，亞特蘭大鷹隊就退役咗佢嘅9號球衣。

佩提嘅遺憾係佢職業生涯大部分時間同塞爾特人嘅王朝重疊——嗰段連霸至今仍然係美國職業運動史上最長嘅王朝之一。

佩提兩度喺總冠軍爭奪戰中僅僅同冠軍擦身而過。佢帶領嘅鷹隊四次打入總決賽，全部對手都係波士頓，當中兩次輸到第七場。

第一次係1957年，塞爾特人喺第七場激戰到雙加時先贏；第二次鷹隊成功封王，終結咗塞爾特人十季九冠嘅壟斷。其後鷹隊喺1960年（七場）同1961年（五場）嘅總決賽再次不敵塞爾特人。

佩提離開籃球後返到故鄉巴頓魯治，從事銀行同財經顧問工作。近年佢經常現身LSU同新奧爾良塘鵝嘅賽事。
